NDT ERP software for inspection companies in Lloydminster

An inspection company based in Lloydminster needs an NDT ERP that handles two provinces, long drives to scattered thermal sites, and technicians who carry Canadian as well as employer-based certifications. The Atlantis ERP solution does that from one system: every job knows which side of the border it is on, every technician's certificates are tracked by scheme and expiry, every instrument is tracked by serial number and calibration status, and every report and invoice ties back to the job that produced it.

The section above lists the operators and regulators in the Lloydminster market. This one is about running the business: how an NDT company here schedules crews across the heavy oil region, keeps certification and calibration evidence ready for pre-qualification audits, writes method-specific reports in the field with no signal, and bills the work accurately. Everything described as built in is in the software today; anything specific to your company is configured during implementation.

If you would rather see it than read about it, request a demo built around Lloydminster work. Atlantis ERP is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a quote on request.

The Lloyd thermal region is where the growth work is

The upgrader and refinery in town get the attention, but a lot of the day-to-day inspection work around Lloydminster sits out on Cenovus's Lloyd thermal projects, a group of steam-assisted heavy oil operations in west-central Saskatchewan that includes sites such as Spruce Lake, Rush Lake, Vawn, Dee Valley and Edam. In 2025 Saskatchewan's Ministry of Energy and Resources approved expansions at the Spruce Lake, Bolney, Sandall and Edam sites, and in 2026 Cenovus announced plans to expand Spruce Lake further. New facilities, tie-ins and expansions mean fabrication, construction and commissioning inspection on top of routine operating work.

For an inspection contractor that is a logistics problem as much as a technical one. Sites are spread over a large area, road conditions change fast in winter and spring breakup, and a technician who is two hours out on a pad cannot be sent to a callout at the upgrader the same afternoon. The Atlantis ERP puts GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates on every team assignment, shows each technician's current assignment and next available date, and records vehicle assignments by project and driver with dates and mileage. Your dispatcher plans with facts rather than a phone call to every truck.

  • Thermal site work: new-build and expansion QC, weld inspection on piping and facilities, thickness surveys, long travel days.
  • Upgrader and refinery work: planned outages and routine operating inspection close to town.
  • Fabrication and service shops: shop inspection for the yards that build and repair equipment for the region.

Two provinces, one company record

Lloydminster is the only Canadian city split by a provincial boundary, and the whole city keeps Alberta time. For an NDT business the boundary shows up in paperwork: pressure equipment is regulated by ABSA on the Alberta side and by the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan on the other, and payroll, workers' compensation and tax obligations follow where the work happens and where the worker is based. A job record that does not say which province it is in will eventually cause a billing or compliance mistake.

In the Atlantis ERP every project carries site, client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope and acceptance criteria, and the site record holds its coordinates. During implementation we configure the province as part of the site and job setup, set up the applicable taxes on quotations and invoices, and use cost centres so you can report revenue and margin by province if you want to. Company certifications, such as quality system registrations or provincial authorisations your company holds, sit in the same system with their own alert days, so an expiring company-level document gets flagged the same way an expiring technician certificate does.

This is not glamorous, but it is the part that small companies get wrong most often, because the knowledge sits in one office manager's head. Putting it into the job structure means a new dispatcher or a new accountant can pick it up without a week of hand-over.

Technician certification tracking software for Canadian and employer-based schemes

Canadian NDT technicians frequently carry certification through the national certification body under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, alongside employer-based qualifications for particular clients or for work in the United States. The Atlantis ERP records each certificate as its own line: scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level from trainee to Level III, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam result and attachments. Status is calculated automatically as active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked.

Vision tests are recorded with near vision (Jaeger J1 or J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry. Examination sheets hold general, specific and practical scores, with a passing score that defaults to 70 percent. Certificate templates per scheme store validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours, so your written practice lives in the system rather than a binder.

The employee NDT profile brings it together: technician flag, highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days ahead of any certificate or vision-test expiry, email alerts go to the recipients you choose with look-ahead and resend intervals you set, and timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid. When a pre-qualification auditor asks for proof that every technician on a thermal-site job was current, you pull it from the job rather than from a stack of PDFs.

Calibration management software that survives a prairie winter

Instruments working around Lloydminster in January live a hard life. Cold cables stiffen and crack, batteries fail early, displays go sluggish, and probes get knocked about in trucks. Asset Management tracks every instrument, probe and source-related item by serial number, with equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories, lifecycle state (new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired, disposed), calibration frequency and status.

Equipment goes out and comes back through an issue and return workflow with supervisor and manager approval and condition recorded both ways, so damage is tied to a date and a job. The maintenance log records preventive, corrective, repair, cleaning, firmware update and probe replacement work with condition before and after. Reservations stop two crews claiming the same serial, inbound and outbound movements are logged, and dispatch warns when assigned equipment is out of calibration.

Calibration records carry provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, pass, fail or conditional result and next due date. The calibration certificate register stores the lab accreditation number, validity status, PDF and expiry alerts. Because calibration labs are not on every corner in the region, many companies ship instruments out for calibration and lose track of them in transit; the in-calibration lifecycle state and movement records show where each unit is. Purchase records link calibration and repair orders to the specific serial, and consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer, magnetic particle media and PPE have reorder levels and low-stock flags.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for long travel days

Team Assignments runs each job from planned to dispatched to in field to submitted to closed, in calendar, kanban or list view. The technician availability calendar records assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable entries and blocks overlaps. Double-booking of technicians or equipment serial numbers is blocked. For each person you see status, current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, and approved Time Off flows into the same calendar.

Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag, rate multiplier, site, client, equipment serial and approval. In the Lloydminster market the travel and standby lines are where money leaks. A crew that drives two hours each way to a pad and then waits on a permit has spent most of its day on non-inspection time, and whether that is billable depends on the contract. Recording it by type on the day, with a billable flag, means the invoice reflects the contract rather than whatever the crew lead remembered on Friday.

Fleet records vehicle purpose, whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources, the transport licence number and expiry, and vehicle assignment to project and driver with dates and mileage. Expenses captures field costs and per diems, which can be re-billed to the job. Together that gives you a true cost of each remote job rather than an estimate.

NDT reporting software that works where there is no cell signal

Plenty of pads in the Lloyd region have weak or no coverage. The offline field app in the Atlantis ERP is an installable web app that stores drafts and photos locally, offers a method picker, photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview, and syncs when the device reconnects, whether that is back at the truck or back in town. A REST API for field devices lists jobs assigned to the technician and equipment issued to them, and handles report submission and sync.

The reporting app covers 17 report types, each with its own numbering sequence: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography. Data is method-specific: UT probe calibration tables, RT source, technique, IQI type and placement, MT technique and particle type, PT method and developer, PAUT focal laws, MFL scan mode and item lines, UT thickness readings by direction, and weld and job lines with defect type and orientation. The overall result is acceptable, not acceptable, or acceptable with remarks, and each report references work order, request, WPS, contract, drawings, procedure and standard.

Reports move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and fields for a third-party or authorized inspector. Versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML carry your logo and headers, and Excel templates can be filled automatically by mapping fields to cells when a client wants its own format. The same engine runs the standalone Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Procedure control with Level III sign-off

The Procedures app keeps a register of document number, revision, method (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, PAUT, LT, AE, hardness, PMI, CR, DR and more), scope, material, applicable standard, acceptance criteria and the procedure text or file. The workflow runs draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, rejection reasons, dated prepared, reviewed and approved-by fields, locked approved revisions and a snapshot of each revision. Approvers get email notifications and reminders.

For cold-weather work this matters. If your PT or MT procedures have a qualified low-temperature variant, the register shows which revision applied on which date and who approved it, and each report references the procedure it used. An AI-assisted first draft can speed up writing a new procedure and falls back to a built-in template, but a Level III reviews and approves every procedure before it is used.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Lloydminster work

Quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, NDT service products flagged by method and category, a global discount and a branded PDF. Clients can accept and sign online and the quote converts into a sales order. Invoices carry NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables, and lines that record cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours.

Billable timesheet hours and their rate multipliers feed billing, and taxes, payment terms and reminders are configured for Canada and each province during implementation. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over 12 months, so you can tell whether remote thermal work is earning its travel costs. Ask for a quote scoped to your crew size.

Integrations, dashboards and the rest of the stack

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, with each integration scoped per implementation. Dashboards show NDT KPIs including calibration due and overdue, certificates expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return, alongside the financial dashboard.

The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, with a 0 to 100 NDT lead score, CSV import and drip email sequences. Business cards from local trade events can be photographed and turned into leads. For asset owners, Atlantis Digital Twins shows inspection data on a 3D model with indication mapping and thickness and remaining-life trends. Trainees can practise on the Practical NDT 3D simulator, and the eLearning app hosts Level I, II and III course content. See every module on the ERP apps page, including asset management and NDT reports.

How a Lloydminster implementation runs

We usually start with technicians, certificates, vision tests and the instrument register, because that is what pre-qualification audits look at first and what goes wrong most often when it lives in spreadsheets. Next comes dispatch with site coordinates and province set up on each site, then the offline reporting app and your report templates, then procedures, quotes and invoicing. Integrations to accounting or client systems are scoped and built last. Atlantis NDT founder Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, reviews the NDT-specific setup. Book a scoping call when you are ready.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a small Lloydminster inspection company?

One system that joins certifications, calibration, dispatch, offline reporting and invoicing is the best fit for a small company here. The Atlantis ERP solution does that, is affordable and fully customizable, and is quoted on request.

Can it track CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification alongside SNT-TC-1A?

Yes. Each certificate records its scheme, certifying body, level, method and dates, so a technician can hold national and employer-based certifications at the same time and each is tracked separately.

Does it handle jobs on both sides of the Alberta-Saskatchewan border?

Yes. Province is set on each site and job during implementation, taxes are configured accordingly, and cost centres let you report by province.

Will the field app work on remote thermal pads?

Yes. It stores drafts, photos and signatures locally and syncs when the device reconnects.

Does the ERP run engineering assessments on client equipment?

No. The ERP runs your company's operations and reporting. Thickness and remaining-life trends can be visualised in Atlantis Digital Twins.

Can it connect to our existing accounting software?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP or any system that accepts API connections, scoped during implementation.

Does Atlantis provide training for our technicians?

Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training. The ERP can record any other certificates your technicians hold, including Canadian national certification.
